analysis.title: More information required: FOMC Post-Meeting Comment October 2026
key_insights: The FOMC held the target range at 3.75-4.00% on Oct 28, 2026. Hammack (Cleveland Fed) and Cook (Board of Governors) dissented in favor of a 25bp hike.
Rabobank had expected three dissents, so the voting members were less hawkish than it forecast. Cook's dissent stands out because President Trump is still trying to remove her from the Fed.

The statement upgraded economic growth from a 'solid' pace in September to a 'strong' pace. It says accumulating more information will help the Committee set the policy stance needed for a timely return of inflation to 2%.

Warsh gave no forward guidance but made the case for a December hike by saying the FOMC will be better positioned to decide at the next meeting after an information-rich interval. Rabobank expects a 25bp hike on Dec 8-9.

Warsh said inflation has been above target for close to 6 years, so the discussion was mostly about the inflation side of the mandate. He said financial conditions have tightened but are not restrictive, and that energy prices have risen again. He called it the Fed's job to prevent relative price changes from broadening out.

The curve steepened between the statement and the end of the press conference. The 10-year yield rose about 3bp and the 2-year fell about 4bp, because Warsh and the FOMC did not sound as hawkish as expected.

Asked whether the AI boom is adding to inflation, Warsh said the economy is strong but not too strong, so AI is not pushing inflation higher. Rabobank reads this as the FOMC focusing on the Middle East supply shock rather than a possible AI-driven demand shock.
Warsh said interest rates do affect AI investment. Rabobank infers that if the FOMC became concerned about AI investment adding to inflation, it might consider additional hikes.
From fall 2027, the FOMC will dedicate one policy meeting a year to monetary policy strategy with no rate decision. Warsh expects two such meetings in 2028. The total stays at 8 meetings a year.
Rabobank's baseline is that the Fed holds through 2027, with a 25bp cut in March 2028 to 3.75-4.00%. It sees upside risk to rates because it expects inflation to rise further in coming months.
The September dot plot median showed one more hike in 2026 and a pause in 2027. With the Iran conflict continuing, the median participant may start to consider an additional hike in 2027.

Warsh denied that the midterm elections next week influenced the hold decision. He dodged a question on Trump's negative opinion of FOMC participants he did not appoint, and said the Fed is not involved in Cook's hearing 'to my knowledge'.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Growth projections for 2026 and 2027 were raised from 2.2% and 2.3% in June.

risk_factors: Inflation is expected to rise further in the coming months, which skews rate risk to the upside.
Energy prices have risen again, and the Fed is concerned about relative price changes broadening into general inflation.
The Iran conflict continues and could push the median FOMC participant to consider an additional hike in 2027.
AI investment could add to inflation, and the FOMC might respond with more hikes if it became concerned.
Political pressure on the Fed, including the effort to remove Governor Cook.
vol_and_positioning: The yield curve steepened during the press conference, with the 10-year up about 3bp and the 2-year down about 4bp.
geopolitical: The conflict with Iran continues and is feeding a Middle East energy supply shock that the FOMC is focused on.
President Trump is still trying to remove Governor Cook from the Fed, and a hearing on Cook is pending.
US midterm elections are next week. Warsh denied they played a role in the hold.

tension_points.bull_case: Hawkish case: Hammack and Cook dissented for a hike, the statement upgraded growth to 'strong', inflation has been above target for close to 6 years, and Warsh signaled the FOMC will be better positioned to decide in December. Rabobank expects a 25bp hike then.
tension_points.bear_case: Dovish case: only 2 dissents versus the 3 Rabobank expected, and the curve steepened as Warsh sounded less hawkish than expected. Warsh gave no forward guidance and said financial conditions are not restrictive.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The information-rich interval before the Dec 8-9 meeting is the test. Data that does not show inflation rising further would undercut the hike call.

theme_stances.key_argument: Without giving forward guidance, Warsh prepared the markets for another rate hike in December.

theme_stances.key_argument: Baseline is the Fed on hold in 2027, but the risks are clearly to the upside as the Iran conflict continues and inflation is expected to rise.
theme_stances.evidence: the risks are clearly to the upside
